newsitem.title: UK: Gold perks up after PGM rally, but seen toppy.
newsitem.headline: Gold perks up after PGM rally, but seen toppy.

text.p: Gold prices reached higher towards the $350 target on Monday on the back of sharp gains in platinum and palladium, dealers said.
Bullion fixed at a one-month high of $348.20 an ounce compared with $345.85 on Friday and with London's close of $345.95/$346.45. Spot bullion then trimmed gains to $347.70.

But the white metals of platinum and palladium stole the limelight, leading a rally on continued delays in supplies from Russia, the world's biggest palladium and second largest platinum exporter, that squeezed the forward market.
Platinum fixed at $395.25, the highest since February 28, with spot prices rising $10.50 to a session peak of $396.50.
The rare metal palladium set the highest fixing since April 20, 1995 of $161.75, up $7.25 from Friday's fix.
"People have been taking metal out of Zurich to meet demand and it's probably running out at the moment. The stocks of metals must be getting thin," said one London dealer.
The move was reflected in high lease rates amid fresh demand from traders to cover immediate needs. One-month platinum was quoted at 14 percent while palladium was lent at a whopping 25.
A Russian finance ministry official said a decree that would allow contract negotiations with key buyer Japan for 1997 to start "has definitely been signed".
But it was still not clear when actual shipments would resume.
But by 1050 GMT platinum had pared its gains to $390.00, still up $4.00, while palladium had edged down to $168.00.
Palladium has been the front runner of a rally triggered by the Russian delays. It gained 51 percent since December 2.
Once the Russian sales resume, dealers expect prices to ease, but not to a dramatic extent due to heavy speculative involvement in the metal.
Gold followed up on Friday's rally that began with the dollar's sharp drop against the yen, shifting some interest from Japan after it had been stuck in the narrow $337.50/$343 range.
The dollar was just off a four month low of 118 yen.
But dealers said gold was beginning to look toppy near $350 after the market breached tough resistance of $345 on Friday.
"I would have thought it's near the top of its range at the moment. I think if you see any reverses in the platinum and palladium you'll see gold come off with them," said another dealer.
Others said pent-up sales from miners who had been waiting for bigger gains in gold were likely to hit the market above $350.
"It's extremely difficult to see what could put up prices as high as $355-$360. Certainly jewellery demand is unlikely to do it," said Ted Arnold, metals analyst at Merrill Lynch.
